newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen up ahead of restructure decision.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen up ahead of restructure decision.

text.p: Shares in German steelmaker and diversified industrial group Thyssen AG climbed nearly six percent in Wednesday bourse trade after its supervisory board said it would decide on Friday on group reorganisation plans.
The stock had already climbed in late Tuesday electronic dealings when the news was released and dealers said bourse dealing was catching up with those gains.

Thyssen stocks were up 14.50 marks at 284 marks in a generally upbeat market, with the DAX index of 30 leading shares, in which Thyssen has a weighting of 1.2 percent, rising 16.79 marks to 2,780.88 marks.

A Thyssen spokesman would not specify the exact changes to be discussed, but described as "speculation" a magazine report which said that any Thyssen units which did not generate returns of 12.5 percent would be restructured, sold off or closed.

A report in the German magazine Manager went on to say that the group was planning to trim back its units to focus on its core business, and that its engineering, coal, petroleum, shipbuilding and steelmaking divisions would be the main focus of the restructuring.
